text_fidelity_a: ATN Shot Trak HD Action Gun Camera Best little on-gun camera I've bought so far.  I got the one without the laser and the one with the laser when it first came out.  The laser is good for short range or indoors, but pretty much a novelty outdoors, in my opinion and experience.  I've shot a lot of videos with this unit already this year, and they came out very well.  The audio is almost too good on my unit.  This microphone picks up almost every single creak and groan and breath and movement within a wide radius.  On several of my videos, it picked up deer walking thru leaves 20 yards away.  I really like how the operator just flips one lever, and then the red light comes on to let them know the unit is recording.  The mini SD card is a little tricky getting in and out, but what did you expect on a compact unit of this nature?  I use a wooden toothpick and gently push the card in to release the catch taking it out and put it in by hand as far as I can, and then I click the card into place with theh toothpick.  Battery life has been good so far, even in cold weather.  I love the fact that the recording magnification is fixed.  No more fumbling around with a zoom trying to get just the perfect magnification.  It is what it is, so just make sure it's recording (and don't forget to take the lens cap off like I did one time) and point and shoot.  It takes videos of deer-sized animals at 50 yards and under very well, and I also shot a nice buck this year with my muzzleloader at 116 yards, and it wasn't bad video at all.  Operator error is drastically reduced.  Also, if you have it indoors and take it outdoors, makes sure to wipe the lens with an scope lens cloth or similar if it fogs up on the outside of the lens.  Had that happen as well.  Again, operator error.  My unit has held up to 12ga 3" slug recoil from a bolt action shotgun, my 50cal muzzleloader, and a 175lb crossbow, and 70lb compound bow so far with no problems.  I paid about $88 on here, and $15 for the memory card (not included).  If you have a weapon that has a rail and you want to video, this is the one to get.  I imagine it would work great for paintball as well.  Buy it.
text_fidelity_b: ATN Shot Trak HD Action Gun Camera

The stitching and leather work is quite nice. It is made in the Philippines. Below is a little information about “Kip Leather”.

Where things get a bit more premium and specialized are the Kip Leather baseball gloves. These can be found in both USA Kip Leather and Japanese Kip Leather. Kip leather is usually the most preferred leather among professional players due to the light, firm, feel and higher quality of the leather. Kip leather comes from younger cattle, which creates a lighter hide that is extremely durable and taut, while also being a little bit easier to break in when compared to USA premium steerhide gloves.

Selecting Your Leather:

Cowhide Leather - Heavy leather, fastest break in time, medium quality, short durability, ideal for youth players.

Steerhide Leather - Heaviest leather, longest break in time, high quality, longest durability, ideal for high school and college players.

Kip Leather - Lighter leather, medium break in time, higher quality, long durability, ideal for college and pro players.

Japanese Kip Leather - Lightest leather, medium break in time, highest quality, long durability, ideal for elite pro players.

text_fidelity_a:
Osprey Unisex-Adult Daypack Backpacks I had a hard time finding a pack to replace my Jansport Penelope 34. I needed something at least that size or bigger and that proved more difficult than expected. I had no idea my pack would be considered so large, it barely fit everything I needed as it is! I only gave it 4 stars because it has only a very small pouch for school supplies. While I understand that it isn't necessarily built for a student, it does have a pouch for a laptop so I guess I assumed it would be more business/student friendly.

In any case, it's large enough but that space is much taller than it is wide. So far, it seems to fit everything I need. I put 2 medium sized text books, 2 spiral bound single subject notebooks, a novel sized book, a 13'' mac in the laptop sleeve and a spiral bound textbook with room to spare. Empty, it's much lighter than my JanSport pack which I appreciate.

It seems to be very well made but I wish it had some of the features of their other packs like the pockets on the waist strap or shoulder straps. It'd be nice to have my phone in front of me instead of in the pack itself but I guess that's what pockets are for. There are 2 stretchy water bottle pockets that seem to accommodate large bottles but they are hard to reach and impossible to put back without taking the pack off. At least that's what I've found out carrying a 1 liter sized bottle today.

The color is gorgeous! I love, love, LOVE it! It's a very deep aqua/turquoise color that's not overly bright or obnoxious. It's seriously one of the nicest looking packs I found in this price range when shopping and I looked at everyone and I mean EVERYONE! I spent about 2 days doing research and this was one of the best deals for the most volume out there. Overall, I think most students would be happy with it but it might be considered very large if you don't pack your books around all day. I carpool so I get dropped off at school in the morning and don't leave until early evening. I need to take all my books, workout clothes, food etc... So this pack still might be a little tight for all that but we'll see.

UPDATED 08/28/14

The bag has held up extremely well. I questioned how the elastic pockets on the front and sides would hold up and they seem to be just fine. After having it for a year I have to say the shape is frustrating. It's too tall and narrow so it wastes too much space. I find myself having to stack things on top of my books to take full advantage of the size of the bag. Other than that, it's been comfortable, kept my stuff dry on rainy days and still looks new! I'm glad I'm graduating in December because I'd probably want to buy another bag and I don't think my husband would appreciate that very much ;-)
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Unisex-Adult Daypack Backpacks

text_fidelity_a:
iBert Child Bicycle Safe-T-Seat My daughter and I love this seat. I bought it because I did not want to haul a heavy trailer.

It is installed on my beach cruiser and it fits perfectly - plenty of room for me to reach the handlebars and pedal without the bike seat in the way. I am 5'4" short. It was easy to install. I am surprised at how stable and natural it feels.

I bought it when she was 10 months old, but she was too small to use it. I started using it when she was just over 1 yr and she fit much better (she is average size).

So far we do short rides around the neighborhood in the evenings and weekends and I can take her 1.5 miles to daycare, and she loves it. She can also look up and see me and ring the bell. We can talk about the things we see on the ride, unlike if we had a trailer.

She has fallen asleep twice while riding. There is nowhere for her head to go, but to slump sideways. I have just supported her head with my hand for the few minutes it takes me to get home.

One very nice aspect to this seat is that it mounts on the bike stem, so when she grabs the handlebars, she can't get any torque to steer the bike.

Mine came with the padding for the seat.

Cons:
The shoulder straps are a little strange - they can slide off her shoulder, but this won't be a problem when she is bigger.

The bar that comes down over the child's lap has a cheap attachment mechanism. This ought to be fixed in the next models - it is not acceptable for a product this expensive.

In a light rain (like we encountered last weekend), water puddles in the bottom of the foot cups - I might drill a hole on the bottom of each one (we live in the Pacific NorthWest).
text_fidelity_b: iBert Child Bicycle Safe-T-Seat

text_fidelity_a:
Timex Unisex The Timex Run Trainer 2.0 is great low profile watch with accurate heart rate monitoring and GPS tracking. It does have several unexpected shortcomings, especially when considering the price and its label as "Ironman".

Nice size. This is one of the smaller heart rate w/ GPS watched I've seen. It fits well, even on my smallish wrists.

Fast connection to GPS - usually took less than 15 seconds, which is pretty good I think.

The memory on this watch is too small, especially considering the price. It seems to hold only about 10 hours of data before it becomes full. Timex should really include a much larger memory chip - aren't they pretty cheap these days?

Biking: Even though there isn't a biking mode, you can switch from pace to speed, which basically makes it a cyclocomputer, in conjunction with the GPS data. You can use the data with online software, including recent support by Strava Cycling.

Swimming: This watch (eventhough it is an Ironman), doesn't technically support swimming. It is waterproof to 50m, which should be good enough for most swimmer. Unfortunately the GPS does not work underwater, even just a foot a water - so you completely lose GPS tracking while swimming. Major bummer. There is a work around I've read about: Place the watch under your swimming cap, so that it usually remains above the water. That seems to help with the GPS, but since the buttons on this watch are very sensitive, you do need to play around with the orientation of the watch so one does not get pressed unintentionally.
text_fidelity_b: Timex Unisex

I ended up returning it.

text_fidelity_a: ENGERWALL Fitness Tracker with Step Counter/Calories/Stopwatch, Activity Tracker with Heart Rate Monitor, IP68, Health Tracker with Sleep Tracker, Smartwatch, Pedometer Watch for Women Men Kids When I got this, I was so excited. It was easy to use, and really encouraged me. I have high blood pressure, so I thought that the 10 thousand steps I was doing every day somehow lowered it. Then I went to my doctor, and found that my blood pressure was higher than ever, despite the fact that the watch said it was below normal. So I took my blood pressure at the doctors office at the same time I took it with the watch. Three times the numbers were drastically different. Then, just out of curiosity, I carefully counted my steps to see if the watch came up with the same number. Not even close.  This is a great tool if you are looking for a way to boost your confidence and self esteem without having to actually improve anything--you know, kind of like the filters in photoshop that make you look thinner and younger. However, if you are wanting accurate information, skip this watch and find one that tells you the truth about your health and fitness.

text_fidelity_a: BIANCHI 7000 Black Sporting Holster Fits S&W K Frame 6 I think I gave about $40 for this holster.  I know there are cheaper and much more expensive holsters out there.  Fits my S&W 22 pistol like a glove.  Two things I don't like about it:  Price is first objection, but it IS a quality product.  The second thing is it has a velcro-type hammer strap that goes from the polymer belt attachment to a snap on the front of the holster.  The thickness of the velcro-backed strap actually takes up space inside the belt attachment.  If you have a thicker belt, it's going to be a tight fit where the strap is and looser on both sides of the strap.  I know it's a bit nit-picky, but I want my belt attachment point uniform from one side to the other.  Overall, it's a great item, and I would recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: BIANCHI 7000 Black Sporting Holster Fits S&W K Frame 6

I bought it to use with rental boats at a local lake. The boats I use the motor with are Jon boats, about 12 foot, and extra wide. The motor has more than enough power. Speeds 1-3 cover the range I like for trolling. On setting 5, it moves the boat along faster than I thought it would - so I can cover distance if I need to. Likewise, the reverse speeds cover the necessary power range. I have used the motor it with 1-3 people in the boat, and performance has been great in all cases.
I use a group 27 Everstart marine battery, and the Minn Kota Trolling Motor Power Center. (I highly recommend buying the power center and the upgraded weedless prop.) After about 5 hours on the lake, trolling and cruising nearly the whole time, I typically have 78 - 85% charge remaining. One could easily use this setup for an entire long day of fishing. With the added weedless prop, I have been able to move through heavy weeds. I only had a problem once in starting from a stop in some heavy growth.
I have been using the motor for two years with no problems. It has been dropped, banged on rocks, etc., and is very durable.
I can confidently recommend this motor.

text_fidelity_a:
Weslo Cadence G 5.9i Cadence Folding Treadmill, Easy Assembly with Bluetooth, 30-Day iFIT Membership Included So, I ordered this treadmill to get exercise during quarantine. I use to swim in a therapy pool but being its the pandemic the pool has been closed. I need exercise, now. I have gained 25 pounds. I have five months until summer.

So, I asked for my treadmill to be delivered to my condo unit. I asked for them to buzz the door so they can wheel it to my door.

That did not happen that way. I got a message on my phone that it was delivered. I took my two wheeler down to the door just incase I needed it. It was in between two doors. (I am 60 years old and have bad knees)

OMG, the box is huge and extremely heavy. So, first I tried to go through the doorway. It wouldn't fit through, So, I got the pail of salt by the door and pulled that over to hold the door wide open. It took several tries but I got it through.

Then I wheeled it down to my door. It is "HEAVY" (I didn't want to drop it) Then I had to get it through my door. I struggled but I got it up and over the door lip.

I got it to the place I wanted to set it up.

The easy part was removing everything from the box.

There is two things when putting this together that you need another person to help. I didn't have anyone so I used a pillow. because you can't lay it on it's side to attached the base, it will make it uneven.

Turned the TV on and watched some you tube videos. I found 2 good ones. One video showed how to assemble it. The other video was how to use it.

Plus I used some of the comments that people made to Amazon on somethings the manual did not state or I didn't want to look through the manual.

So, I found the on/off switch. It spelled out HELLO, so I than pressed the Bluetooth button for 20 seconds and it's all set to go!

It works fantastically. I love it so far.
text_fidelity_b: Weslo Cadence G 5.9i Cadence Folding Treadmill, Easy Assembly with Bluetooth, 30-Day iFIT Membership Included

text_fidelity_a: DR.VIVA Fitness Tracker Watch, Heart Rate Activity Tracker Touch Color Screen IP67 Waterproof Sport Tracker Watch with Calorie Counter Pedometer Sleep Monitor for Kids Women Men I got this in exchange for my honest review.  This is a love hate relationship.  I love the features and all the different settings but I hate the interface.  Sometimes screens scroll super smooth and respond to touch inputs as they shoul and sometimes they wont scroll or lag so bad you want to smash this with a hammer.  Sometimes it links seamlessly with the phone and sometimes you canset it on top of the phone and it acts like it has never even haerd of bluetooth.  There is no rhyme or reason.  I used it in a workout yesterday and part way thru i must have bumped the screen because it turned off the fitness program.  Today it would not register i was working out at all.  Some of the data is super accurate (im wearing a second fitness watch just to compare) and some is so far off that according the the watch I may just be deceased (not really but i dont see my heartrate reaching 276 bpm just sitting watching videos)  The app is ok but does take some getting used to and some stuff that should be intuitive seems awkward and reversed.  They use odd terms for certian actions (like to unpair or disconnect from the phone they use the term unbind! )  There are a lot of nice features but are almost to specific (like there is no workout routine but you can choose tenmis, soccor, running, badmiton, basketball etc.).  And it stores messages (i thimk up to 5) but if you dont delete them new messages are not displayed only the old ones.  The band is real nice and the watch looks like a very expensive timepiece.  Charging was straight forward and batterylife was excellent.  The watch did get caught in an upgrade loop that kept telling us there was no devise connected.  We unbound and rebound the watch and it settled down.  There is a lot to do and set with this watch and when it is working it is really nice.  Patience is sometimes needed to work with it at times.  What i saw and used with this watch I really liked  and the app is a pretty good app once you get beyond some of awkward language
text_fidelity_b: DR.VIVA Fitness Tracker Watch, Heart Rate Activity Tracker Touch Color Screen IP67 Waterproof Sport Tracker Watch with Calorie Counter Pedometer Sleep Monitor for Kids Women Men

I fill them about half way with ice then top with water, and they are still icy the next morning, and sometimes even the next day after work (about 18 hours later). The flip-up lid is great for 1-handed use. The little plastic ring, while looking a little weak, has actually stood up very well. The rubber grip and otherwise textured surface makes them easy to hang onto during long walks. I've never had the slightest problem with leaking or spilling. We absolutely love these, and will continue using them daily for years to come.

Update, reduced rating to 3 Stars:
My wife and I have been using these bottles daily for about two and-a-half years. After about a year, both bottles' vacuum seals failed, so water will no longer stay cold overnight, even when filled completely with ice right before bedtime. They also sweat almost immediately after filling. For the price, I'm really not thrilled that these didn't last longer. Further, the seal between the cap and bottle has proven to be less than adequate, as it lets some moisture out into the cap's threads every day. I have an older model Thermos with a screw top which came with a much better seal, that's still good after 5+ years, plus its vacuum seal is still intact despite being dropped several times.
text_fidelity_b: Under Armour Dominate 24 Ounce Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Bottle with Flip Top Lid

text_fidelity_a:
SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Presta Valve Tubes, Multiple Sizes I ordered two Sunlite (Kenda) Thorn resistant tubes (700c x 18/23) with removable presta core in July of 2015. I wanted a thick (puncture resistant) tube that allowed me to remove the core (with a chain tool) to allow me to inject tire sealant into the tube.

In the Southwest, we have nasty thorns called 'goatheads' that cause many flats. As part of my defense system, I use: 1) a thick, thorn resistant tube, 2) tire sealant (Flat Attack); 3) a high-quality, super puncture-resistant tire (Schwalbe - Marathon Plus Tour, Marathon Supreme, or Durano Plus - depending on the bike).

I waited a while to see how these Sunlite tubes would hold up. Unfortunately, after about a year and a half, the front tube failed. The presta valve stem separated from the tube, rendering the tube unrepairable and useless. The rear tube got a flat, but due to the tire sealant, I was able to simply pump up the tire, spin the wheel, and it sealed itself.

I had high hopes for these tubes, but I will look for other alternatives.

TIP: One reason that many of these tubes may be failing at the stem is due to the threaded, round 'nut' on the valve stem. The nut is really helpful when inflating the tube for the FIRST time, (i.e., when there is no air in it). However, once inflated to full pressure, I would recommend REMOVING this nut and setting it aside. The problem is that when riding with this nut tightened down on the valve stem, it creates added pressure on the stem at the base of the tube, increasing the likelihood of separation & failure.
text_fidelity_b: SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Presta Valve Tubes, Multiple Sizes

Planet Bike Beamer 3 Bike Headlight This light has two practical safety functions:

It helps make your presence on the road more apparent to on coming traffic. The light is bright enough from even a few hundred feet that a driver would have to be extremely oblivious and distracted not to see it.

Perhaps more importantly, the light will illuminate street signs and signals that are made with a reflective material at distances of over 450 feet away (I measured using google maps). When I first used the light (in flashing mode), I was genuinely shocked to see how the street signs up to two blocks ahead of me were pulsating. I say that this is important because it helps you spot stop signs in the distance - assuming you're being a safe cyclist, biking in a lane, with traffic, abiding by traffic laws, you're probably most likely to get killed by accidently running a stop sign. When I bike home from work at night, I take streets that have no traffic lights and only stop signs, so being able to spot them is very important for me.

The light attaches to your handle bar through via a mount; the light can easily slid off the mount so you don't have to bike around with it during the day, nor leave it on the bike when it's parked outside.

The light does what it needs to do for a reasonable price. I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.

text_fidelity_a:
Slumberjack Tough Cot (32 x 82 x 19-Inch) We have several 4WD truck camping trips coming up this Spring, Summer, and Fall. We wanted to move from inflatable mattresses to cots in our 10' x 8' Kelty Ridge 6 tent. We were looking for a durable, comfortable cot that set up easily, left plenty of room for storage below the bed, was at least 32" wide, and could easily support 250 lbs without feeling like it was always on the verge of collapse. We tried several cots that cost anywhere between $40 and $150. The more expensive cots were comfortable and fit our needs, but we were having a tough time justifying the price. We were starting to rethink the move to cots until we both laid on the Slumberjack Tough Cot, a cot rated to 350 lbs. We bought two immediately at a local sports warehouse because it fit all our parameters for a great price.

When we opened the boxes we realized there are no instructions with the cots. Still, it took us less than five minutes to figure out how the cot sets up, including proper installation of the end-cap support bars. Once we had the process figured out the second cot took less than a minute to set up. Breakdown and stowage back in the bag takes maybe three minutes.

The cot is solidly constructed with very little sway when set up. The bed material is tough. Yep, the cot is heavy, but hey, we're not backpacking. We picked up a 3"x32"x82" foam pad for $20 at a local hardware store, cover it with a sheet, throw down the sleeping bag, and crawl in for the night. Camping can often be an exercise in sleep deprivation due to the lack of comfort. NOT WITH THESE BABIES! My wife and I both LOVE sleeping on these cots with the foam pad mentioned. It feels downright decadent compared to the blowup mattresses we used to use. The Slumberjack Tough Cot was one of the best purchases ever for our camping fun.

We're looking forward to years of use from our Slumberjack Tough Cots.
text_fidelity_b: Slumberjack Tough Cot (32 x 82 x 19-Inch)

text_fidelity_a:
Piscifun Fishing Pliers, Saltwater Fishing Pliers with Split Ring, Fish Hook Remover, Corrosion Resistance Fly Fishing Pliers with Braid Cutters, Sheath and Lanyard, Fishing Gear Gifts for Men Overall they are worth the purchase price. However there are some cons, listed below, that you should consider.

Pros: They are functional to a point. They seem to be well built. I used them on a recent fishing fly-in fishing trip to handle a variety of fishing tasks and they did not bend of fail to operate at any time. The pouch is convenient.

Cons: The split ring "nose" on the end makes it difficult to remove hooks when the fish has swallowed the bait. It actually causes additional damage as you have to push the tip in further to get the second side engaged with the hook. As mentioned the pouch is convenient, but the retention strap causes more issues then benefits. I found I had better luck leaving them outside the pouch while seated in the boat and across my leg. Then when I left the boat I put it back in the pouch and messed with the retention strap.

Is the tool overall useful? Yes, and for the price it's a good idea to have on hand while on the water. Can improvements be made - absolutely!
text_fidelity_b: Piscifun Fishing Pliers, Saltwater Fishing Pliers with Split Ring, Fish Hook Remover, Corrosion Resistance Fly Fishing Pliers with Braid Cutters, Sheath and Lanyard, Fishing Gear Gifts for Men

text_fidelity_a:
Conquer Indoor Bike Trainer Portable Exercise Bicycle Magnetic Stand This trainer is a very basic, low friction (Light workout) trainer that is very easy to set up.
It is solidly made, and very quick to assemble (really no assembly)
Very nice that it comes with wheel quick release rear wheel skewer to fit the trainer, and front wheel stand.

However, for low noise & a hard enough workout I ended up buying:
> The red trainer tire: Slick for no noise $40
> A shimano cassette that has a tiny 11 tooth high gear $20
> Small 26" tube and rim tape to support the tiny red tire $7

Note: don't make the mistakes of did. I bought a second wheel for $40 to have a quick change from quiet trainer to road-worthy. My bike has a 7 speed Shimano back cassette. The new wheel had a 7 speed Shimano FREEWHEEL WITH 13 teeth high gear. They both work on this bike, but do not share inte changeable cassettes. A "freewheel wheel" is cheaper & weaker- the way the bearings support the axle. (Per good Sheldon brown webpage). And I had to adjust all the derailleur stops to have it shift properly on the freewheel wheel. I needed a 11 teeth high gear to get a good workout, so had to move the red tire & tube to the old wheel with cassettes & get a 11tooth to 28 tooth cassette.

Finally loving my quiet workouts!!!

So, this is a very basic entry level trainer because it has:
> Light drag for the rear tire; just a little magnet drag; no air drag squirrel cage; no flywheel; no fluid drag system. Just a light magnet drag.
> No quick release to get bike on & off; must screw these bolts in & out and fine tune.\
> no quick release for roller pressure on rear tire. Bend down and screw it in trial & error for enough drag without much noise.

About noise:
For me it was a balancing act to get enough of a workout without overtightening the roller which creates a lot of tire squeaking/ deforming noise. I tried tire pressures from around 50 up to the max of 87psi. Still hard to get a lot of trainer drag without slick tire squeaking/ clicking noise.
1. It is not really that the TRAINER that makes any noise at all. It is quiet, but creates very little drag with it's little one-setting magnet.
2. A TIRE with ANY tread will generate noise. Even at a slow low gear for Physical Therapy for an ACL injury, my neighbors were looking over the fence for the strange noise.
3. With a SLICK tire, the noise ranges from near zero (with just enough roller pressure so the tire will not slip on the roller), to "Pretty squeaky/ clicky-noisy" if you press the stainless roller too much more into the tire to increase the workout intensity. The tire simply deforms so much around the roller it has to squeak and slide around, making a pretty loud clicking sound.
Edit: I realized the tire only squeaks loudly a couple mnutes, then gets totally quiet when it warms up. These tire "clicks" sound so mechanical I could have sworn they were coming from inside the roller /drag mechanism. But it's the tire / roller slip that goes away when it gets warmer & stickier.
4. So the actual noise occurs even with a slick tire if you want a hard workout because the stand has very little built in magnetic friction. No flywheel/ no air or fluid drag. So for a light workout it can be quiet. (I'm going to my highest gear on my 21 speed to get more drag)
5. A partial solution for me is to change shimano cassettes and go from a 13 tooth highest gear to a 11 teeth high gear. This makes the wheel spin faster> harder workout> still low enough roller pressure on red trainer tire to be very quiet (only chain & sprocket noise).

I read other reviews saying they wished the bought a better trainer. After a day using this, I understood why. (Low drag on this one, no quick release roller or bike holder, Also, the magnetic drag is sort of a clicky on & off drag ,as if your chain is contributing vibration into your ride; but it's really the magnet drag working properly. So air drag or fluid drive trainers can create a lot more drag without the little clicks, and a flywheel on a better model trainer makes for a more realistic ride feeling
text_fidelity_b: Conquer Indoor Bike Trainer Portable Exercise Bicycle Magnetic Stand

text_fidelity_a:
Esbit Ultralight Folding Pocket Stove with Six 14g Solid Fuel Tablets steel, Small - Original Used this during a 2 day hike in a cave in the southeastern US. At ambient 58F near ~2,100' AMSL, 1 Esbit 14g fuel tablet just brings 1.5l of water to a boil before burning out. They claim 12 min. burn time. I only observed around 8~9 min, but it did what I needed, was smaller and lighter than propane canisters, etc. Fuzzy guess says the cost per pot heated is similar to propane, with these being a bit more trouble/less flexible, but smaller and lighter.

Compared to Trioxane, these tablets seem to have about ~30% more energy per tablet, but that's just this backpacker's impression. They're harder to light than trioxane, but not overly difficult.

This little stove has a slightly wider base than the old US Army issue Trioxane stoves. This makes balancing a pot on it much easier. Note that canteen cups don't balance well -- it's just a bit too wide for them to fit comfortably. You can sort of jam one in, but it's precarious and falls over if you so much as sneeze at it. This makes sneezing at your canteen cup highly discommended. A great loss, to be sure.

text_fidelity_a:
Lifepro Waver Mini Vibration Plate - Whole Body Vibration Platform Exercise Machine - Home & Travel Workout Equipment for Weight Loss, Toning & Wellness - Max User Weight 260lbs I’ll be honest, I’d never heard about exercise plate machines until I saw this one. I looked it up and according to the articles I was reading, this is an under used exercise machine type and actually does help loose weight. So I decided to grab this LifePro Waver Mini Press Vibration Plate Exercise Machine and try it. I come away surprised, but happy - it does help me. My wife and I have been active in living a healthier lifestyle and approach with a variety of activities, from kickboxing and walking to weights to... well, this thing. My wife is still sidelined from her severely broken foot, so she has not tried it yet, but I have and I’m blown away by how it works.

The machine arrives in a box that is easy to remove from - all the parts are fit correctly and easy to get out. It is slightly heavy - nothing one can’t move, but it has some weight to it. I’m not sure the actual size, but we can’t fit it under our bed, so we’re still working on where to keep it - but that’s not an issue. There are instructions - I would suggest also doing a little research. I learned a few things from articles I was reading. There are also resistance bands and for your arms resistance ropes as well. The instructions are well done and offer ideas for working out as well.

The unit has a remote so you don’t have to get off or bend down to alter things. I have used it every time - I will increase or decrease the various options while still on it. This comes in handy for severity of the vibration as it is intense and I’ll inch it up or down during the workout. I have not gone very high - I want to say around 15 - and appreciate being able to try things or adjust as I need.

ONE CON: The power cord is short. I have to use it primarily in our bedroom where my wife is currently working from bed, so that limits when I can use it. If it were at least another 2 - 3 feet long it would be perfect. I’m going to move some things around and try to make it work in the living room, but if not... anyways, if they changed that this would be a perfect unit.

I really love the workout. It is... (not) easy. I mean you’re standing on this vibrating plate and you do feel it. The level, the time, going up and down, the truth is, your body works to stay there. I’ve only stood on it and done planks, and both were workouts. I got off sweating. I’ll say, standing on it is less of a vibration to my head than the plank - I can’t go as long or as high at a single time because in the plank position I feel like my head will vibrate off. But I can feel my core working.

I like this unit so much that when I saw a foot massager from the same company I grabbed it. While you can use this as a foot vibrator, I thought to help my wife heal - when cleared by the doctor - she might be able to use that foot massager to advance her healing - but again, I grabbed that because of this company - I was that impressed.

Overall the LifePro Waver Mini Press Vibration Plate Exercise Machine is a great workout tool and we are happy to have it. I feel like it has added to my workout and will aide me in getting into the shape I’m working towards and my goals.
text_fidelity_b: Lifepro Waver Mini Vibration Plate - Whole Body Vibration Platform Exercise Machine - Home & Travel Workout Equipment for Weight Loss, Toning & Wellness - Max User Weight 260lbs
